title: Fix docs/site/index.md YAML frontmatter regression causing VitePress build failure
description: The docs/site/index.md frontmatter was accidentally broken by commit 6e0d94c28 (validate-videos PR, #319). That PR stripped the proper 2-space indentation from all keys under hero: and features:, and reverted the closing --- back to -------------------------------------------------------------------. VitePress's YAML parser then sees two top-level 'text:' keys (one from hero.text and one from the first action's text) and throws: YAMLException: duplicated mapping key at line 11, column 1. This is blocking the release pipeline — the 'Build documentation for GitHub Pages' step fails and the entire release workflow aborts. The fix is to restore the correct indentation (2 spaces for hero/features children, 4 spaces for action items) and the proper --- closing delimiter.
acceptance_criteria: docs/site/index.md has properly indented YAML frontmatter; VitePress builds without error locally and in CI; the fix is committed and pushed to release/2.X.X
close_reason: Fixed in 29ae217b0 (docs/site/index.md YAML indentation restored) and pushed to release/2.X.X

title: Match detail view: active injuries not applied to wrestler effective HP
description: In the Match detail view, active injuries are not reducing the wrestler's effective HP as expected. For example, a wrestler with 'Dislocated Shoulder - Severe (4 health penalty) (Active)' still shows their maximum HP value in the effective stats panel — the injury penalty is being ignored entirely. This means matches are adjudicated with incorrect stats, giving injured wrestlers an unfair advantage and breaking the injury system's impact on gameplay. The health penalty from each active injury should be subtracted from the wrestler's base HP when computing effective HP in this view, consistent with how effective stats are calculated elsewhere (e.g. the Player view).
close_reason: Fixed in this sprint — injuries now correctly reduce effective HP in match detail view.

title: Fix null showId NPE crashing segment sync

Fix: guard with early return before calling syncShow when showExternalId is null.

title: Fix ShowSyncService: parse ISO 8601 timezone dates

Notion sends dates as ISO 8601 with timezone (e.g. 2026-01-12T00:00:00.000+00:00) but the parser expects plain yyyy-MM-dd. Fix: try OffsetDateTime.parse() first, fall back to LocalDate.parse(). File: ShowSyncService.java lines 547-553.

title: Fix ShowSyncService: don't skip shows when ShowType relation is null

title: Add Prettier-based Spotless formatter for docs/site markdown to prevent YAML frontmatter regressions
description: docs/site/** is currently excluded from the Spotless markdown formatter (pom.xml <markdown> section). This means docs/site/index.md's YAML frontmatter is never validated or auto-fixed by Spotless. The result was two incidents where the frontmatter lost its indentation (once fixed in 7efc5124a, then reintroduced in 6e0d94c28 by the validate-videos PR). The fix is to add a new Spotless <markdown> section using <prettier> (same prettierVersion 3.3.3 and .prettierrc.json as the TypeScript step) targeting docs/site/**/*.md files. Prettier understands YAML frontmatter and auto-corrects indentation on mvn spotless:apply, preventing the regression from ever reaching CI.
design: Add a second <markdown> block in the Spotless config (separate from the existing flexmark block) using <prettier> with prettierVersion 3.3.3 and configFile pointing at .prettierrc.json. Include docs/site/**/*.md. Exclude target/**, node_modules/**, node/**. The existing flexmark block excludes docs/site/** so there is no overlap. Test that Prettier does not mangle VitePress-specific syntax (::: tip blocks, <DownloadLinks /> Vue components, ## headings in body).
acceptance_criteria: mvn spotless:apply reformats docs/site/index.md to have proper 2-space indentation in frontmatter; mvn spotless:check fails if frontmatter is unindented; VitePress build still succeeds after Prettier formatting; no regressions in generated guide pages

title: Non-blocking AI narration: offload provider calls to background threads
description:
## Problem

AI narration generation and image generation both block the entire Vaadin UI session, making the application unresponsive while AI HTTP calls are in flight (typically 5–60+ seconds including retries). Navigation to other tabs is impossible during this time.

## Root Cause

All AI-invoked code paths call providers synchronously on the Vaadin UI (HTTP request) thread. Because Vaadin holds a session lock per request, no other server interactions can be processed for that user during these calls.

---

## Affected Call Sites

### Segment Narration (worst offender)

| Location | File | Line | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| MatchView.generateAiNarration() | MatchView.java | 1044 | Direct blocking `narrateSegment()` on UI thread. The `ui.access()` at line 1050 only wraps the result callback, not the wait. |
| NarrationDialog.generateNarration() | NarrationDialog.java | 333 | Blocking `segmentNarrationController.narrateSegment()` via REST on UI thread. Also calls `narrateSegmentWithProvider()` at line 692 with same pattern. |
| AbstractSegmentNarrationService | AbstractSegmentNarrationService.java | 232–248 | Synchronous entry point; delegates into retry loop |
| AbstractSegmentNarrationService | AbstractSegmentNarrationService.java | 370–416 | callAIProviderWithRetry() uses Thread.sleep() for backoff — up to 5 retries × 30s |
| ClaudeSegmentNarrationService | ClaudeSegmentNarrationService.java | 90–139 | HttpClient.send() — blocking HTTP |
| OpenAISegmentNarrationService | OpenAISegmentNarrationService.java | 101–148 | HttpClient.send() — blocking HTTP |
| GeminiSegmentNarrationService | GeminiSegmentNarrationService.java | ~90 | HttpClient.send() — blocking HTTP |

### Image Generation

| Location | File | Line | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| GenericImageGenerationDialog.generateImage() | GenericImageGenerationDialog.java | 144 | Direct blocking `service.generateImage(request)` on UI thread. All three image UIs route through this method. |
| ArenaFormDialog | ArenaFormDialog.java | 175/289 | Button click → opens GenericImageGenerationDialog → blocking |
| NpcListView | NpcListView.java | 128–140 | Grid button → opens NpcImageGenerationDialog (extends Generic) → blocking |
| NpcProfileView | NpcProfileView.java | 131–140 | Button click → opens NpcImageGenerationDialog → blocking |
| OpenAIImageGenerationService | OpenAIImageGenerationService.java | 81 | HttpClient.send() — blocking HTTP |
| PollinationsImageGenerationService | PollinationsImageGenerationService.java | 98 | HttpClient.send() — blocking HTTP |

### Not in scope (already async or non-UI)
- Notion sync services in `service/sync/` — called from Spring `@Scheduled` tasks, not the UI thread
- `NotionHandler` — called from background sync contexts
- `GameSettingsView` calling `notionHandler.reinitialize()` — reinitialize is fast config wiring, not a slow API call

---

## Required Changes

### 1. Enable @EnableAsync (Application.java)
Add `@EnableAsync` to the Spring Boot application class. Spring's `SecurityContextHolder` is already configured to `MODE_INHERITABLETHREADLOCAL` (Application.java line 51), so security context propagates automatically.

### 2. Async wrapper for segment narration
Add `CompletableFuture<String> narrateSegmentAsync(context)` annotated `@Async` in `AbstractSegmentNarrationService` (or factory). Calls existing `narrateSegment()` internally.

### 3. Refactor MatchView.generateAiNarration() (MatchView.java ~line 817)
```java
UI ui = UI.getCurrent();
narrationServiceFactory.getBestAvailableService()
    .narrateSegmentAsync(context)
    .thenAccept(generated -> {
        if (generated \!= null && \!generated.isEmpty()) {
            ui.access(() -> {
                narrationArea.setValue(generated);
                segment.setNarration(generated);
                segmentService.updateSegment(segment);
                updateCommentaryDisplay();
                notificationService.showSuccess("Narration generated\!");
                ui.push();
            });
        }
    })
    .exceptionally(ex -> { ui.access(() -> notificationService.showAIServiceError(ex)); return null; });
```

### 4. Refactor NarrationDialog.generateNarration() (NarrationDialog.java ~line 320)
Same async pattern. Move `showProgress(false)` into completion/error callbacks instead of the finally block.

### 5. Async wrapper for image generation
Add `CompletableFuture<String> generateImageAsync(request)` annotated `@Async` in `AbstractImageGenerationService` (or interface). Calls existing `generateImage()` internally.

### 6. Refactor GenericImageGenerationDialog.generateImage() (~line 112)
```java
UI ui = UI.getCurrent();
// disable button, show spinner
imageFactory.getBestAvailableService()
    .generateImageAsync(request)
    .thenAccept(imageData -> ui.access(() -> { /* update preview, enable save */ ui.push(); }))
    .exceptionally(ex -> { ui.access(() -> showError(...)); return null; });
```
This single change covers all three image UIs (Arena, NpcList, NpcProfile) since they all route through this dialog.

### 7. Loading state that does not block navigation
For all async calls: disable the trigger button before dispatch, show a spinner, re-enable/clear in callbacks. NarrationDialog already has `showProgress()` — adapt it. GenericImageGenerationDialog needs one added.

### 8. Test coverage
- Unit test: mock async service returns completed future; verify UI update callback fires
- Integration test: verify `@Async` executes on a different thread than the caller
- Cover both narration and image generation paths

---

## Effort Estimate

| Task | ~Hours |
|---|---|
| @EnableAsync + narrateSegmentAsync() wrapper | 1h |
| Refactor MatchView async | 2h |
| Refactor NarrationDialog async + progress state | 2h |
| generateImageAsync() wrapper | 0.5h |
| Refactor GenericImageGenerationDialog async + spinner | 1.5h |
| Tests (unit + integration, both paths) | 2h |
| Manual smoke test (all providers, narration + image) | 1h |
| **Total** | **~10h (~1.25 dev days)** |

---

## Acceptance Criteria
- Clicking Generate (narration or image) does not freeze navigation to other views/tabs
- A loading/spinner state is visible during generation
- Successful result is applied to the UI on completion
- Errors surface as notifications without crashing the view
- All existing narration and image-generation tests pass
acceptance_criteria: Clicking Generate does not freeze navigation; loading spinner shown during generation; result inserted on completion; errors surface as notifications; existing tests pass
close_reason: Implemented: @EnableAsync, narrateSegmentAsync/@Async override, generateImageAsync default, MatchView/NarrationDialog/GenericImageGenerationDialog all async. PR #330 open against release/2.X.X.

title: Fix two MatchView.beforeEnter crashes: LazyInitializationException and AuthorizationDeniedException
description:
MatchView.beforeEnter fails with two distinct errors causing E2E test failures in PlayerViewE2ETest, MatchNarrationE2ETest, MatchDetailsE2ETest, BookerDocsE2ETest, and GameMechanicsDocsE2ETest.

Bug 1 — LazyInitializationException (MatchView.java:275):
autoAssignRefereeIfNeeded() does `segment = segmentService.updateSegment(segment)`. The returned entity has Show as a lazy proxy (session closed), so Show.getName() throws LazyInitializationException in buildHeader(). Fix: drop the `segment =` reassignment — the original local segment already has Show eagerly loaded from findByIdWithDetails.

Bug 2 — AuthorizationDeniedException (MatchView.java:232):
For league matches (not campaign or universe), canUserUpdateSegment() returns false for PLAYER-role users, so updateSegment() throws Access Denied. Fix: guard the save with isAdmin()||isBooker() since referee auto-assignment is a management function.
close_reason: Referee auto-assignment now uses runAsAdmin() as a system operation. Both LazyInit and AuthorizationDenied issues fixed and covered by MatchViewAutoAssignRefereeIT.

title: Add checksum safeguard for released Flyway migration scripts
description:
Released migration scripts (those at or below the version in .released) must never be edited. Today's production outage was caused by exactly this — scripts were modified after being applied to prod, causing Flyway checksum validation failures on startup.

Need to add a fast, always-running safeguard:
- At release time, generate a checksum manifest (e.g. db/migration/h2/.checksums and mysql/.checksums) listing version→SHA-256 for every script <= the version in .released
- Commit the manifest as part of the release workflow
- Add a unit test (MigrationChecksumTest or similar) that reads .released, reads .checksums, and verifies current file hashes still match
- Test runs on every mvn test with no database or Docker needed — fails in seconds if a released script is touched
- Update release workflow to regenerate manifests when cutting a release

title: Audit and fix Show, Faction, Title, League list views for universe filtering
description:
Verify that ShowListView, FactionListView, TitleListView, and LeagueListView consistently filter by the current universe. Fix any that don't.

## Why
These repositories already have findByUniverse methods, but the views may not be using UniverseContextService to pass the right universe in. A systematic audit is needed.

## What to implement

title: Inbound show sync only inserts, never updates existing shows

title: Fix SegmentSyncService: strip time suffix from Notion dates
description: SegmentSyncService expects dates in 'MMMM d, yyyy' format but Notion sends '@January 21, 2026 12:00 AM' — the time suffix causes 632 DateTimeParseException warnings per run. The @ prefix is already stripped (line 268). Fix: also strip everything after the 4-digit year using replaceAll('(\w+ \d+, \d{4}).*', '$1') before parsing. File: SegmentSyncService.java lines 267-284.

title: Fix Notion tests leaving entities on live servers (issue #331)
description: Notion integration tests can pollute the live Notion workspace when NOTION_TOKEN is set in the environment. Two gaps: (1) mock state from TestNotionConfiguration leaks between test classes sharing a Spring context; (2) tests that use a real NotionHandler (NotionTokenSettingTest) have no guard to skip when no real token is available, and no cleanup if they do run live. Fix: add @NotionLiveTest annotation with @EnabledIfSystemProperty guard, add NotionTestCleanupExtension JUnit 5 extension that archives tracked page IDs after live test runs, and reset the shared NotionHandler mock in AbstractIntegrationTest.baseSetUp().

title: MenuService: derive item visibility from @RolesAllowed on route views
description:
## Why this issue exists

MenuService currently hard-codes role requirements on every MenuItem constructor call. Whenever a view's @RolesAllowed changes (or a new view is added), the developer must remember to update MenuService too — this is what caused the Campaign menu to still show for PLAYER/BOOKER after the views were tightened to ADMIN only (ATW-art).

## What to implement

Introduce a RouteRoleResolver service that maps route paths to their required roles by scanning all @Route-annotated Spring beans for @RolesAllowed at startup. MenuService then uses this resolver to enforce visibility instead of (or in addition to) manually supplied roles.

### Suggested approach

1. Create RouteRoleResolver (or add logic to MenuService directly):
   - Inject ApplicationContext
   - On first call, scan all beans that carry both @Route and @RolesAllowed
   - Build a Map<String, Set<String>> of routePath → required roles
   - Cache the result (routes don't change at runtime)

2. Update filterMenuItem in MenuService:
   - For a MenuItem that has a non-null path, look up the path in the resolver map
   - If roles are found, use them to gate visibility (union or intersection with any manually-specified roles, TBD in design)
   - If no annotation exists on the target view (@PermitAll or unannotated), treat as open

3. Remove (or make optional) the role varargs from MenuItem constructors for paths that are now auto-resolved — keeps MenuService lean and self-consistent.

### Design decisions to make
- **Merge strategy**: if a MenuItem has both explicit roles and auto-resolved roles, use the intersection (stricter) or union (more permissive)? Recommendation: intersection — the view annotation is the source of truth; explicit menu roles can only narrow further, never widen.
- **@PermitAll handling**: treat as no restriction (everyone can see the item).
- **@DenyAll handling**: always hide the item.
- **Children with no path**: parent items with null paths (group headers) keep their explicit role list as a fallback.

## Acceptance criteria
- Adding @RolesAllowed(ADMIN_ROLE) to a view automatically hides its menu entry from non-admins without any change to MenuService
- Removing the explicit roles from a MenuItem for a routed view does not break visibility logic
- Views annotated @PermitAll remain visible to all users
- Existing manually-specified roles on parent group items (Entities, Configuration, etc.) continue to work as a coarse filter
- Unit test: MenuServiceTest verifies that a mock route with @RolesAllowed("ADMIN") is hidden for a PLAYER user and visible for an ADMIN user, without any explicit role on the MenuItem
close_reason: RouteRoleResolver implemented, MenuService updated, full test suite (unit + E2E) passing, pushed to feature/ATW-fzt-menu-role-resolver

title: [Phase 4 discovery] Investigate existing expansion/admin settings model
description:
Before implementing per-universe expansion settings, understand what expansions are and how the current admin settings work.

## Why
The user confirmed that the admin settings have expansion toggles that should be per-universe. We need to understand the existing model before designing the per-universe layer.

## What to investigate
- Search for 'expansion' in all entity, service, view, and migration files
- Identify what an expansion is: is it an enum, a DB table, a config file, or something else?
- Find the current admin settings UI and how expansion toggles work today
- Determine which entities (wrestlers?) are scoped by expansion
- Check if there is already any per-universe or per-league differentiation of expansion availability
- Document the findings as notes on this issue before any implementation begins

## Deliverable
Update this issue with notes describing:
- What expansion is in this codebase (class/table names, key fields)
- How expansions are currently toggled (admin settings flow)
- What a per-universe expansion settings model would look like
- Any complications or existing patterns to follow
notes:
## Findings

### What is an Expansion?
An expansion is a named content pack defined in src/main/resources/expansions.json. It is a plain JSON object with name and expansion_code fields, deserialized into the Expansion POJO (service/expansion/Expansion.java). There are 9 expansions today: BASE_GAME, EDDIE, EXTREME, MATT_CARDONA, RUMBLE, TRAILBLAZERS, ATW_VS_WOW, GAIL_KIM, HURT_BUSINESS.

Each Wrestler and Npc entity has an expansion_code column (defaulting to BASE_GAME) tagging which expansion they belong to. Teams inherit expansion scope from their member wrestlers. Factions filter by members expansion codes.

### Global (Admin-level) Expansion Toggle — current state
ExpansionService reads enabled state from the game_setting key-value table using keys like set_enabled_CODE. Toggling via ExpansionManagementView (a tab inside AdminView) calls ExpansionService.setExpansionEnabled(), which saves to game_setting and publishes ExpansionToggledEvent. NpcService and TeamService listen to that event and evict their caches. Default when no row exists is enabled.

### Per-Universe Expansion Override — already exists!
UniverseExpansionSetting entity (table universe_expansion_settings, migration V78/V46) stores (universe_id, expansion_code, enabled) with a unique constraint. UniverseExpansionSettingRepository has findByUniverseAndExpansionCode, findByUniverse, and deleteByUniverseAndExpansionCode.

UniverseSettingsService already implements the full override layer:
- getExpansionsForUniverse(universe) — returns all expansions with per-universe enabled state
- isExpansionEnabledForUniverse(universe, code) — checks override row first, falls back to global
- setExpansionEnabled(universe, code, enabled) — saves/updates override row
- resetExpansionToGlobal(universe, code) — deletes override row to revert to global

UniverseFormDialog already wires this in the UI: it renders an expansion grid with checkboxes calling settingsService.setExpansionEnabled(universe, ...).

### The Gap — what ATW-46y must fix
All runtime content-filtering (WrestlerListView, FactionService, TeamService, NpcService) still calls ExpansionService.getEnabledExpansionCodes() (global only). None call UniverseSettingsService.isExpansionEnabledForUniverse(). Per-universe settings can be stored but have no runtime effect.

### Implementation Plan for ATW-46y
1. Add getEnabledExpansionCodesForUniverse(Universe) to UniverseSettingsService — mirrors getEnabledExpansionCodes() but resolves per-universe overrides
2. Inject UniverseContextService + UniverseSettingsService into FactionService, TeamService, NpcService
3. Replace getEnabledExpansionCodes() calls with the new universe-aware method using the current universe
4. WrestlerService.findAllFiltered already accepts universeId — extend the expansion check to use UniverseSettingsService with that universe
5. WrestlerListView filters by a single expansionCode string — change to a Set of enabled codes per universe

### Complications
- ExpansionToggledEvent is only fired by the global toggle; consider a UniverseExpansionToggledEvent for per-universe changes so caches evict correctly
- No circular dependency risk: UniverseSettingsService depends on ExpansionService, not the reverse
- WrestlerService.findAllFiltered post-filters in memory, so adding universe-aware expansion check is a low-risk in-place change
close_reason: Investigation complete — findings and implementation plan written to issue notes

title: Reduce CI test execution time with predictive test selection or path-based job filtering
description:
## Context

The full test suite (unit + integration + E2E) is slow to run in CI. The project already has profile separation (`-Pintegration-test`, `-Pe2e`) and JaCoCo coverage data. The workflow already uses `dorny/paths-filter` with coarse `code_changed` and `notion_changed` outputs — every E2E job fires whenever anything in `src/**` changes, including pure backend changes that cannot affect the browser UI.

Launchable (ML-based test selection) and Develocity (build cache + predictive selection) are both paid products. This issue focuses on free improvements only.

## Approach: Granular path filters (no new tooling, no cost)

The existing `check-paths` job can emit additional outputs that gate each job more tightly. Proposed additions:

### New filter outputs

```yaml
ui_changed:
  - 'src/main/java/**/ui/**'
  - 'src/main/java/**/view/**'
  - 'src/frontend/**'
  - 'src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/**'
  - 'package.json'
  - 'package-lock.json'
  - 'tsconfig.json'
  - 'vite.config.ts'

service_changed:
  - 'src/main/java/**/service/**'
  - 'src/main/java/**/repository/**'
  - 'src/main/java/**/domain/**'
  - 'src/main/java/**/rest/**'
  - 'src/main/java/**/controller/**'

db_changed:
  - 'src/main/resources/db/**'
```

### Job gating changes

| Job | Current gate | Proposed gate |
|---|---|---|
| e2e-tests | code_changed | ui_changed |
| docs-e2e-tests | code_changed | ui_changed |
| validate-video-tests | code_changed | ui_changed |
| notion-e2e-tests | notion_changed | notion_changed (unchanged) |
| integration-tests | code_changed | service_changed OR db_changed |
| build-and-unit-test | code_changed | code_changed (unchanged — always run) |

E2E jobs are by far the most expensive (require Chrome, frontend build, Spring Boot startup). Skipping them on pure backend/service changes gives the biggest wall-clock win.

### coverage-and-analysis guard

The coverage merge job uses `needs` on all test jobs. When a test job is skipped its result is `skipped` not `failure`, so the `if:` condition on coverage-and-analysis needs to allow `skipped` results for optional jobs. This is already partially handled; verify the condition covers the new gating.

## What this does NOT do

- Does not drop any tests permanently
- Does not require any paid service or external account
- Does not change test profiles, Surefire config, or test code
- Full suite still runs on every push to `main` and on release tags (code_changed is always true on those paths)

## Effort estimate

~2h: update `check-paths` filters, update each job `if:` condition, verify `coverage-and-analysis` guard still works for skipped jobs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A PR that only changes service/domain code does not trigger E2E jobs
- A PR that only changes a Vaadin view does trigger E2E jobs
- A PR that changes DB migrations triggers integration tests
- Full suite still runs on push to main and release tags
- coverage-and-analysis job succeeds even when some test jobs were skipped
notes: Came up while investigating E2E test failures. JaCoCo already runs; Launchable can ingest its data. Launchable has an open-source free tier worth checking before committing to a paid plan.
close_reason: Implemented granular path filters in maven.yml: ui_changed gates E2E jobs, service_changed/db_changed gates integration tests. coverage-and-analysis updated to tolerate skipped jobs.

title: Automate prod dump generation in release workflow for MySQL migration tests
description:
FlywayMigrationIT already has a prodDumpMigratesSuccessfully test that validates new migrations apply on top of a real MySQL database, but it is opt-in and manual (-Dprod.dump.file=...). This means it never runs in CI.

Need to:
- Add a step to the release workflow that generates a sanitized MySQL dump at the .released schema state and commits it to the repo (e.g. src/test/resources/db/prod-snapshot.sql)
- Wire CI to run FlywayMigrationIT with -Dprod.dump.file pointing to that committed snapshot on every build where db/migration/mysql/ changes
- The dump should be sanitized (no real PII) but representative — enough rows in key tables to trigger NOT NULL, UNIQUE, and FK failures if migrations are wrong
close_reason: GenerateMysqlSnapshotIT generates sanitized mysqldump at .released state; release.yml runs it and commits the snapshot; CI integration-tests job auto-detects the committed snapshot and passes -Dprod.dump.file to FlywayMigrationIT when it exists

title: Fix HTTP error codes swallowed by catch block in image generation services
description: OpenAIImageGenerationService and PollinationsImageGenerationService both have a try/catch(Exception e) that re-wraps any thrown AIServiceException (including ones thrown for non-200 HTTP responses) as a generic 500. This means a 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden from the upstream API always surfaces as 500 Internal Server Error to callers, losing the original status code. The fix is to either catch AIServiceException separately before the general Exception catch, or rethrow it without wrapping. Discovered while writing unit tests for ATW-asl.
